content.text: Quote confirmed verbatim. Submitting the repaired finding with the quote re-anchored on the term length and the express "for any reason" convenience right.

input.quote: The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale: Compliant at the playbook fallback; no redline. A Customer convenience right is expressly present: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — a termination "for any reason" is termination for convenience, so the phrasing differs from the playbook's "for convenience" wording but is substantively identical. Ninety (90) days sits at the outer edge of the fallback's 60–90 day notice window. Term structure: a one (1) year Initial Term with 1-year auto-renewals, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in — AP has a rolling 90-day exit from the end of year one onward. The mid-Initial-Term bar ("Neither Party may terminate ... during the Initial Term") is symmetric and equally restrains Kubient from walking away on AP mid-term, so it partly benefits our party and is not flagged. No early-termination fee or penalty falls on AP: Kubient is entitled only to fees "generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue actually earned across the 90-day notice period while it continues performing, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap rather than a penalty. Vendor convenience right is available only following the Initial Term and on exactly ninety (90) days' notice — not "fewer than 90 days" — so it stays out of walk-away territory. Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted rather than escalated per the playbook's classification semantics: 90-day rather than 30-day notice; Kubient's right running any time after the Initial Term rather than only at the end of a renewal term; and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is inapplicable because §5 (p0023) is a revenue-share under which payments flow from Kubient to AP within 7 days of receipt, so AP prepays nothing capable of refund.
